context: Warehouse and workshop workers routinely stack and rack parts whose weight is not centred, such as tubes with fittings or tools with heavy heads, and must find each part's real balance point by feel. Here three bars with hidden off-centre weights go on a post narrower than the bars, so each must rest on its own balance point, and every bar added shifts the load on the ones below. Placing them at their geometric centres makes the stack tip.
fidelity: Rigid boxes stand in for aluminium tubes with sealed steel weights, keeping each bar's off-centre centre of mass and inertia. Friction is estimated (bars 0.6, post 0.5); there is no denting or breakage model. Arm joint torque limits are 27 N m (joints 1-3) and 7 N m (joints 4-6), including gravity. The link load limit uses a conservative bound (normal plus friction force). Not calibrated against hardware.
instruction: Stack the three bars on the narrow steel post: orange at the bottom, blue in the middle and purple on top. Each bar has a sealed steel weight inside, so it does not balance at its middle. Lay each bar level, with its length running front to back (away from the arms), resting only on the bar or post below it. Then let go of all three so the stack stands on its own for the last 20 seconds.
reset_notes: Return all three bars to their start poses on the table (same fixed layout and masses every episode, no random offsets) and the arms to their ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,896 steps); demo: 1.0 (1,441 steps, final stack held 25.2 seconds)
scoring: At the end of the run, find the longest stack, A, A+B or A+B+C in that order, that has met all of the following conditions continuously for the last 20 seconds, and score 1/3, 2/3 or 1 for it; otherwise 0. A must rest on the post, B on A and C on B, and each of these bars may touch nothing except the bar or post directly below it and the bar directly above it in that stack. No robot part may touch any of the three bars; any such contact restarts the 20-second count. Each bar's long axis must be within 0.06 rad of horizontal and within 10 degrees of the x direction (either way), one of its square side faces must be level within 0.06 rad, and it must be still: the norm of its linear (m/s) and angular (rad/s) velocity together below 0.025. The whole run scores 0 if a wrist force stays above 80 N for 100 ms, if an arm touches a bar while its gripper is outside the allowed workspace (x -0.05 to 0.60, y -0.55 to 0.25, z 0.7725 to 1.1275 m), or if any measurement is invalid. A wrist force above 30 N for 20 ms, or a load above 50 N averaged over 20 ms on any arm link other than the fingers, stops arm motion until it clears. task/contract.py gives the exact tests.
setup: Coordinates in metres: x forward from the arm bases, y left, z up. A fixed oak-look table (1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m) is centred at (0.36, 0, 0.7175), top at z 0.7475. Three loose bars lie on the table, each a 320 x 50 x 50 mm aluminium square tube with a sealed steel weight inside and black plastic end caps; the black cap marks each bar's -x end (the end nearer the arms at the start). All long axes start along +x. Orange A: centre (0.25, -0.45, 0.7725), 666.4 g, centre of mass 52.4 mm from the middle toward +x. Blue B: centre (0.25, -0.34, 0.7725), 777.5 g, centre of mass 86.2 mm toward -x. Purple C: centre (0.25, -0.23, 0.7725), 682.1 g, centre of mass 75.4 mm toward +x. A fixed, bolted steel post (28 x 30 mm, 160 mm tall) is centred at (0.25, 0.03, 0.8275), top at z 0.9075. Two six-joint YAM arms with parallel grippers (40 N finger drives) have base origins at (0, +/-0.305, 0.97), facing +x, each on a fixed steel riser (140 x 140 x 213 mm) centred at (0, +/-0.305, 0.854). There are no other loose objects. Inertias, friction values and camera placement are listed in the README and task/inventory.json.
title: Build an ordered balance chain with three eccentric bars
